POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: As a child you were noticed for being capable, and help at home was something you earned. Because managing alone won you approval early, people still meet that capable face first, and friends trust you to carry your share. Asking your family or anyone else for something has stayed the hardest thing you do, and you go without more often than the people around you guess.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Your first home expected you to manage, and you were trusted with your own problems before most children are. Because you were trusted young, you came to trust yourself before anyone else, and you worked out much of what you know without asking. The habit makes it hard for you to let people in, at home or anywhere, and you accept help only after you have tried it alone.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You built your working life on your own effort, and the people around you have always seen it. Because doing it yourself is how you stay sure of your worth, you take whole tasks and sign your name to them, and you stall wherever credit is shared loosely. You keep your equals close at work, and you have quietly let go of everyone who treated you as junior.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Under everything you do at work sits a need to own it, the skill and the result and the name on it. Because depending on anyone feels like losing yourself, you have built your working life on effort nobody else can claim. You learn the same way, slowly and in full, until a skill is yours to the last detail. You finish later than you would beside one trusted colleague, and you accept the delay as the price of owning the result.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: At home you want two people deciding and neither one in charge, and you lose patience with a partner who leans on you for every choice. Because equality is how you feel respected, you track who conceded the last argument, and you rarely say so. Your friendships run on the same level terms, and you keep the friends a partner also respects. You grow easier about being looked after once someone has proved they stand level with you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you run your own affairs and turn down help politely, and the people around you notice. Because standing on your own is how you show who you are, children or younger relatives or someone you train learn self-reliance from watching you. You go on learning new skills long after most people stop. You pay for that independence with a distance the young find hard to cross.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Twin inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you keep company only where you are met level, with old friends who became family and with children or younger relatives or someone you train who speak to you as equals. Because dignity matters more to you than comfort, you turn down help that comes with pity. You keep learning through the few people who still argue with you. The circle gets smaller as the decades pass, and you lean on the ones who remain more than you admit.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: People who knew your first home remember its nerve and its charm, the way it won over a crowded table. Because boldness was praised at home, people warm to you quickly, and you act while others are still deciding. You learned to spend as fast as you earn, much of it on friends, and you feel uneasy holding on to money for long.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: As a child you shared a bed or a bike or a birthday with a sibling or a cousin who wanted their turn. Because nothing at home stayed yours for long, you learned to give quickly and to keep a quiet count. Your family reaches for your help and your money first, and you say yes before you have worked out what it costs.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You volunteer whenever there is a contest to enter, and the colleague who ranks first is the one you watch. Because winning in the open is how you prove your worth, you climb quickest where results are ranked and stall where credit is pooled. You make friends and allies through the same contests, and you lose some of them as quickly as you made them. Your worst setbacks have come through bets you shared with someone else.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Underneath what you do for a living is a need to have something at stake, and waiting has always felt riskier than acting. Because you measure yourself against the people beside you, you do your best work where results are counted in public and shared with partners. Your colleagues and your friends end up as one circle, and your income arrives in surges that you spend on them as fast as it comes. You build more than you keep, and it rarely troubles you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You are drawn to bold partners with strong opinions and their own way with money, and a mild love has rarely held you long. Because you feel most alive when someone pushes back, your home is lively and loud, full of debate and shared bets. Money is where the two of you clash most, since you both want your way. You keep the peace best where each of you holds an account of your own, and the arguments turn back to love.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: Your later years stay bold and public, and you keep taking risks long after people your age have stopped. Because being in the contest keeps you feeling alive, you say yes to children or younger relatives or someone you train more than you planned, and their ventures keep you learning. You find real joy in some of that backing, and you lose part of what you give because you say yes before you ask what it is for.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Rival inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: Your later life stays loud and full, with children or younger relatives or someone you train arguing with you and for you. Because you value being matched more than being obeyed, you are drawn to the bold ones, and you give them more than you promised yourself. You share most of what you build late, and you hold on to your part only where you fixed its size early.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Affection reached you early and without effort, from the older relatives around you and from children you had only just met. Because being liked came so easily, you expect a welcome wherever you go, and you usually get one. Your body has run well on regular meals and sleep, and you feel the cost of too many late nights later than your friends do.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: As a child you were fed well, in more than one sense, and that early comfort still sits under the way you live. Because ease was given to you before you had to earn it, you recover through simple things, food and a full night's sleep and the company of people you love. Whatever else your first home held, you took from it a store of warmth you have drawn on in every hard season since.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Much of what you produce looks effortless to the people around you, and most of it is simply work you enjoy. Because enjoyment is what drives you, the jobs you like go well for you and the ones you only endure stall. Colleagues and friends find you easy company, and that ease has brought you more openings than ambition has. You coast through a smooth year without noticing, and you feel the cost only when it ends.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You do your work quietly and without fuss, and over the years you produce more than people who make more noise. Because your energy comes from sleep, food and routine, your work rises and falls with how well you are living. You do your best in making, feeding or teaching, and you keep improving at it long after others have peaked.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You are happiest where food, rest and easy company are part of every day, and you choose a partner who enjoys them with you. Because ease makes you feel safe, you look after the people you live with through meals and small favours more than through words. Your relatives and friends end up at your table, and you give so much to the household that your own rest comes last.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life people see you cooking, mending or teaching for others, and children or younger relatives or someone you train pick up your skills along with your generosity. Because being useful puts you at ease, you keep making things for the pleasure of it and passing on what your hands know. Comfort that asks nothing of you is the one thing that slows your work, and you notice it in the weeks with no one to make anything for.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Artisan inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you get to enjoy the comfort you have worked for, and your home fills with younger people and long friendships. Because care has always meant a good meal and a warm bed to you, you keep feeding whoever comes, whether they are children or younger relatives or someone you train. Ease is both the reward of those years and their one risk, and you stay well for as long as your days keep a rhythm.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: In class you spotted the flaw in a lesson and said so before the teacher had finished. Because your mind moves faster than others expect, the company you keep sorts quickly into those who enjoy you and those who resent you. Teachers and older relatives were the first to feel both reactions, and you have done better each time you picked your own friends and your own work.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: You asked why before most children do, and the habit of doubting first has stayed with you. Because you learned early to trust your own judgement over what you were told, you have grown fastest in places that let you test things for yourself. Some in your family took your honesty for defiance, and you are closest now to the relatives who heard you out.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Your talent is the first thing colleagues see, and your patience with rules is the last. Because you need your work to be judged fairly, you shine under bosses who reward results and stall under bosses who want obedience. Your friends are the people who enjoy your sharpest remarks, and you have lost a few who did not. You have walked away from at least one job that wanted you quieter.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You spot the better version of a plan, a process or a piece of work almost at once, and the weaker version nags at you for days. Because an unfixed flaw weighs on you more than hard work does, you keep improving things long after others call them finished, and you are still thinking about them at night. Managers find you tiring and colleagues find you useful, and you are proud of being both.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You want a partner quick enough to argue with and warm enough to praise you, and you lose interest in anyone who only agrees. Because being understood is how you feel loved, you say exactly what you notice at home, and the sharpest of it lands on the person you care about most. Your best ideas get worked out in those arguments, and you think more clearly beside someone who pushes back than on your own.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you do your boldest work, at a point when most people expect you to ease off. Because saying the true thing matters more to you than a title, you speak more freely each year, and some who hold rank resent it. You keep changing while there is something new to learn. You pass your talent to the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, along with your dislike of being told what to do.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Virtuoso inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you keep making things and saying what you think, and you look for younger people who will take you on. Because being heard has always kept you well, the ones who stand up to you become your favourites, whether they are children or younger relatives or someone you train. Your family gets your sharpest wit and your newest plans, and you stay closest to the ones who also get your warmth.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: You grew up in a family that spent on guests, gifts and new plans, and everyone who visited could see it. Because money moved freely in the house you grew up in, you learned to spot a chance quickly and to hold cash loosely. That ease with risk has served you well, and you still give faster than you keep.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Someone in your family left home to look for something better, and you grew up hearing about it. Because moving was part of how your family got by, you feel most alive in unfamiliar places and most at rest when you come back. Your best chances with money come from far off, and you have always needed a fixed home to return to.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You find work and money through people, the tip and the contact and the good timing. Because chances reach you that way, you spend your working years meeting people, and your circle and your income grow together. Money comes in through friends and movement, and it leaves the same way, through gifts and plans that drift. You are richest in the years when some of each windfall stays put.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You sense where prices and people and fashions are heading before most of the people around you, and you build your work on that instinct. Because you trust it more than any plan, you earn in waves, with strong seasons followed by flat ones. Each good run makes you want a bigger one, and the gains go back into the next chance. You keep most in the years when someone patient holds what you bring in.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You want a home life with somewhere to go in it, and you are drawn to people whose world is wider than yours. Because your openings come through the people closest to you, love and opportunity arrive together for you more often than for most. Your home years open wider than any before them, and you share them with a person whose world is bigger than your own.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life younger people seek you out, because you keep finding openings long after most people have settled. Since a fresh start keeps you sharp, you take on a new field or a new venture when others your age are winding down. The people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, get more of your time and money than you planned. You are remembered for what you started more than for what you kept.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Horizon inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you want plans on the calendar and people arriving from far away. Because new places and new company keep you lively, a quiet year weighs on you more than a busy one, and you spend on trips without much counting. Those who come after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, pick up some of your restlessness as your family gathers in bursts. You count those gatherings as your real wealth, and you pay for most of them yourself.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: You grew up where money was spoken about plainly and spent with a plan, and that order was the first thing people saw in your family. Because care with money reached you as safety, you still feel calm when the accounts are in order and uneasy when they are not. You still run every budget on the habits you formed before sixteen, and they are why your savings grow when others stall.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: You took in your family's habits with money before you could name them, and they still shape how you feel about spending. Because thrift felt like safety when you were small, you save quietly and early, and your money grows in ways other people mistake for a windfall. Your relatives remain the people you turn to first, and they turn to you. Under the calm sits a small worry about running short, and you carry it even in good years.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You are handed the budget, the accounts and the jobs that need order in every place you work. Because being relied on is how you prove your worth, you take on other people's messes and sort them without fuss. Your income rises on a steady schedule, and your standing rises with it. You are needed everywhere at work, and you are thanked less than you are used.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You want to build something that lasts, a skill kept up and savings that grow each year. Because you trust only what you have earned yourself, you turn down quick gains that would ask you to become someone else. Your progress at work looks slow at first and surprises people later. The cost is a tight grip, and you take less pleasure in what you have built than it could give you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You love by providing, with the bills paid and food in the house on ordinary days. Because steadiness is how you feel safe, you want a partner who values upkeep as much as you do. The cost comes when care turns into chores and the warmth goes quiet. The people you love come to rely on the calm home you keep, and you are proudest of that.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you pay your own way, even when the middle years scatter your plans. Because keeping things in order is how you show care, the habits you hold turn into calm accounts and settled debts after your late forties. You teach the people after you about money mostly by example, and you leave your family more than numbers.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Steward inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you want things settled, with savings kept, care arranged and nothing left to chance. Because providing is how you love, you make arrangements for others long before they are needed, and you keep your own sleep and meals in the same good order. Those who come after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, learn thrift by watching you. Your hardest task in these years is enjoying what you have secured, and you come to it slowly.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Your early life carried pressure that others could see, a demanding home or a tough school or a name you had to defend. Because you were tested young and in public, people learned to respect you early, and authority came to you sooner than to your friends. That start made you hard to push around, and you still take the measure of every new group or job before you settle into it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Your first home asked a lot of you as a child, and you gave it more strength than anyone thought to ask about. Because you had to be strong early, you learned to stay calm in a crisis and uneasy when life goes easy. The same strength left a habit of carrying everything alone, and you still keep your tiredness to yourself. Each hard stretch since has added to what you can carry, and you are steadier for it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Authority shows on you before you say a word, and you are handed the hard jobs early. Because you meet pressure head on, you rise fastest in work with real stakes, and the crises that break others build your name. The friends you keep are mostly people who went through a hard stretch beside you, and colleagues respect you before they warm to you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Easy work has bored you since your late teens, and you went looking for the demanding course or the tough job or the role others turned down. The strain you took on built your ability faster than comfort could have, and your standing grew through it. You have rarely rested before a job was finished, and your sleep and your energy are what that pace has cost you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You are drawn to a partner whose will is as strong as yours, and a calm match has not held you for long. Because pressure is what makes you feel alive, your home life runs hot, and a fight that runs for days shows first in how badly you sleep. You stay longest with a partner who pushes in the same direction as you, toward the work and the home you are building together.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: You keep working under pressure in later life, and people go on bringing you the hard problems because you still take them. Because demanding work is how you know you matter, stopping feels like losing your place, and you keep growing in how calmly you carry the load. You set the standard for the people who come after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, and they respect you more than they relax around you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The General inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: In later life you keep habits others let slip, the early start and the standard kept. Because being strong is how you feel safe, you push on past the point where others would ease off, and rest comes hard to you. The younger ones in your life, children or younger relatives or someone you train, feel protected by you more than held. You grow each time you take on something hard, and your strength holds because you use it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: You grew up in a household known for doing things properly, and its rules were kept in public as well as at home. Because that reputation came with you, your word was believed early and responsibility found you young. The name has its price, and you have always felt the pressure to live up to it. You carry your family's standing into every group you join, and you behave in it as if the neighbours were still watching.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Rules in your first home were felt more than spoken, and you took them in before you could name them. Because order meant safety to you when you were small, you formed a firm sense of right and a strong conscience early. The same conscience keeps a close record of your mistakes, and guilt reaches you faster than it reaches most people. You still measure yourself by the standards you learned at home, and you do best wherever the next step is written down.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Your record speaks for you, and the answer it gets is responsibility and rank. Because you are seen as correct and dependable, titles come to you in steady order, and they stay. In your circle you are the one made responsible, the person others call when something must be done properly. Your name matters more than your pay in these years, and over time it raises your pay as well.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You feel most yourself with a clear role and a job done properly, and you look for that in every place you join. Because steady reliability earns trust, your responsibilities grow year by year, and each new rank teaches you what the last one could not. Among friends you end up making the plans and keeping the dates, and you are relied on more than thanked.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You want love that is committed and clear, with a partner whose word holds as firmly as yours. Because keeping promises is how you show care, you judge a partner from the start by what they do on ordinary days. Over time that seriousness turns part of your love into routine, and the warmth goes quiet before you notice. The home you build with a partner becomes the steadiest place in your family, and you keep it that way on purpose.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: Your judgement is still wanted long after a job has ended, and the requests grow with each decade. Because doing things properly is how you earn your place, you take on roles of trust in later life and fill them with care. The ones who come after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, measure themselves against your example. In your circle and at home your name is one people rely on, and you keep it in good order.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Magistrate inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: You want your affairs settled and your debts paid, and an unanswered letter stays on your mind until it is done. Because keeping your word is how you feel at peace, you finish what you owe before you allow yourself to rest. The ones who come after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, trust that your arrangements will hold. Your growth in later life comes from the few things you value, done a little better each year.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Adults noticed early that you learned differently from other children, and some of them were unsure what to make of it. Because you took in the world on your own terms, teachers found you older than your years and other children found you hard to read. That early difference still shapes how people see you, thoughtful and selective and slow to open up. You let a few friends close in place of a crowd, and you have not regretted the trade.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: As a child you were loved through books or silence or an adult who cared for you in ideas more than in hugs. Because you learned early to feed your own mind, you have depended on yourself for understanding ever since. You grew up through odd subjects and unlikely teachers, at a pace nobody at home could set for you. Time alone still restores you in a way company never quite does, and you are used to being slightly apart.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: Colleagues have seen your odd angle since your first jobs, and they bring you the problems that have beaten everyone else. Because your thinking catches what training does not teach, you are paid for insight more than for hours, and you do your best work with quiet and freedom. The same oddness keeps you outside the circle that hands out promotions. You are remembered for the problem you solved, and you are left out of the meeting after it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You do your real thinking alone, on questions most people find strange, and your work is built on it. Because you trust what you have worked out yourself more than what you were taught, you look quiet from outside while the real work happens inside. You found your important teachers off the usual path, and you are slowly becoming the odd teacher someone else needs.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You want someone near and a door you can shut, and you work out what you feel on your own before you say it. Because your thinking runs in private, you bring a partner conclusions more than first reactions, and anyone who reads your quiet as coldness wears you down. You have learned to explain early that the silence is about the problem in front of you. From your mid-thirties you share your home with someone who values how you think.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: You become known for a rare kind of knowledge, and people with odd problems come looking for you. Because your insight keeps growing with use, your strongest ideas and your most valued work come after your late forties. The younger people who seek you out, children or younger relatives or someone you train, learn from you what no course offered them. You are consulted far more than you are kept company, and your method stays unwritten for longer than it should.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Alchemist inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: Past your late forties your days gather around a few deep interests and a household that respects a closed door. Because you trust what you have worked out alone, your understanding gets clearer with each decade, and you grow by narrowing your attention. Younger people, children or younger relatives or someone you train, reach you one at a time and get your thinking slowly. You are hardest to reach on the very days someone needs you, and you know it.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage at the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Someone with clear principles raised you, and it showed early in your manners and in the way you spoke to adults. Because learning was valued at home, teachers took to you early, and help arrived each time you needed it. Older people still trust you on sight. You expect shelter to appear when things go wrong, and you are slower than most to build your own.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Year Gate
POSITION.value: Someone in your first home gave you decent, patient care, and the ease it gave you became the way you meet the world. Because care reached you early, you trust people first, and you find the protective ones quickly. The same safety made leaving it hard, and you have stayed in comfortable places longer than they helped you grow. You still sleep and eat better after a hard season once you are back with the people who love you.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage at the Month Gate
POSITION.value: The people above you at work take you seriously early, because you have the facts and a steady manner. Their trust moves your career through reputation and study more than through pushing, and you learn whatever they are willing to teach. Your friends come to you with their problems for the same reason. You give a great deal of calm away, and you are rarely the one anyone thinks to look after.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Month Gate
POSITION.value: You keep studying long after the people around you have stopped, and what you know sits under everything you do. Because learning is how you feel safe, you prepare thoroughly for every step, and you wait to feel ready before you put yourself forward at work. Your ability has outrun your confidence for years, and the people who taught you saw it before you did. You grow at your own careful pace, and you are usually the last to see how far you have come.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Day Gate
POSITION.value: You want a home that feels safe before it feels exciting, and you are drawn to partners who are steady more than dazzling. Because being cared for close up settles your sleep and your mood, you do your best everywhere else when home is calm. That comfort has a cost, because you stay in a safe arrangement long after it stops asking anything of you. From your mid-thirties you keep a gentle household, and you start returning the care you are given.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage at the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: Because care and knowledge are what you have to give, you pass them on freely, to children or younger relatives or someone you train. Most of your growth in later life comes through teaching, and it sorts out your own thinking as much as anyone's. Your family treats you as the person to call when something goes wrong. You hear other people's troubles far more often than anyone asks after you, and you feel that on quiet evenings.

POSITION.canonical_name: The Sage inside the Hour Gate
POSITION.value: Accepting help feels strange to you, because for most of your life you have done the looking after. In later life help reaches you anyway, as care from children or younger relatives or someone you trained, and you learn to take it slowly. Your days settle into steady routines of reading, rest and good company, and your mind stays clear on them. You feel smallest in the weeks when nobody needs anything from you, and you rarely say so.

mech: Two of your five energies add to you. Body is more of your own element, and Mind is the element that feeds it.
In your chart these two have your birth season or your roots behind them. Your core takes in more than a day can spend.
The other three spend you. Expression lets your energy out, Action puts it to work, and Order gives it a shape. They are the outlets your surplus is looking for.
gifts: You carry a heavy load without asking for help.
You stay steady under pressure, and you recover fast.
You trust your own judgement and act on it.
costs: You grow restless when nothing asks much of you.
You feel sure you are right, and criticism lands hard.
You hold other people to your own pace and standard.
scenes: A hard deadline brings you alive. An easy month leaves you rebuilding things that were never broken.
A free weekend fills with projects by Saturday noon. Doing nothing feels heavier to you than doing too much.
A friend asks for advice, and you hand over the whole plan. You find it hard when they take only half of it.
value.helps: Give your extra force a place to go — aim it, don’t store it.

mech: Body and Mind add to you. Expression, Action and Order spend you.
In your chart neither side has the stronger claim on your season and your roots. Your core takes in about what it spends.
The classics treat this as the condition the other two work toward. None of your energies needs to grow or be released.
gifts: You fit many settings without losing yourself.
You recover quickly after a hard stretch.
You can push hard or hold back, as the moment asks.
costs: Nothing pushes you to your limit, and you need your own reasons to go further.
A hard year tips you more than it tips others.
You weigh both sides for a long time before you choose.
scenes: You can lead a project or support one, and both feel natural.
A busy week and a quiet week both suit you, as long as neither runs too long.
Friends bring you their problems, because you take neither side too fast.
value.helps: Intake and burn hold each other; protect the equilibrium.

mech: Three of your five energies spend you. Expression lets your energy out, Action puts it to work, and Order gives it a shape.
In your chart these three have your birth season or your roots behind them. Your core spends more than it takes in.
The other two add to you. Body is more of your own element, and Mind is the element that feeds it. They are the intake your chart is asking for.
gifts: You read people quickly and adjust to them.
You make a little go a long way.
You work well beside others, and you share credit easily.
costs: You doubt yourself, even when the work is good.
You start strong and run out before the finish.
You give out more than you take in, and you tire without noticing.
scenes: You say yes to the extra project. Then you carry it alone in your evenings.
A quiet morning with nobody asking for anything feels like a treat. For you it is fuel.
The right mentor or friend changes everything for you. With their backing you finish what you start.
value.helps: Take in what feeds you — intake isn’t a crutch, it’s your engine.

TG_PATTERN.value: There is a rarer wiring underneath this: stress reaches you pre-processed. Deadlines that grind other people turn into output in your hands, and your calmest work happens closest to the pressure. That composure is produced, and it costs fuel. Protect the rest, the craft, and the small pleasures that produce it, and pressure stays your employee.

TG_PATTERN.canonical_name: The Virtuoso harnessed by the Sage
TG_PATTERN.value: Underneath runs a lucky pairing: your boldest ideas and your patience for study feed each other instead of fighting. Every credential sharpens the showmanship, every performance keeps the learning honest. Build the stage and the library in the same decade. Together they turn raw shine into a name that lasts.

One catch runs underneath: your own analysis can starve your output. Projects polish in private until the moment passes, and the drawer of nearly finished things grows. The cure is structural, deadlines you did not set, collaborators who ship, one craft done with the hands. In heavy thinking seasons, watch sleep and appetite first.

One friction runs underneath: you keep correcting the very structures you climb. Under close supervision you dim and chafe, and your brightest work appears wherever the leash is longest. Choose formats that license your candor, your own practice, your own desk, a title with give in it, and the friction becomes reform.

A stronger current runs underneath: hardship keeps converting into wisdom and rank for you. Each heavy chapter has left you promoted, certified, or deeper, usually all three, and the pattern strengthens with age. Trust weight to be a ladder. Just rest between climbs, because the converter needs cooling.

One law runs underneath your money: it attracts company. Friends with ventures, family with needs, partners with opinions, and it thins wherever ownership blurs. The same people would also carry you through droughts no bank would. So formalize every shared asset, price your generosity yearly, and keep one account whose shape nobody knows.

A generous wiring runs underneath: what you make converts to money with unusual ease. The work that feels like play earns more than the work that feels like duty, and the conversion improves with age. Keep one channel where creating flows straight to earning, and guard your appetite to make. Your income lives downstream of it.

A steady engine runs underneath: what you earn keeps converting into standing. Results banked become titles offered, and property and position reinforce each other through your middle decades. The one flaw is under-asking. Negotiate rank as deliberately as you earn it, and make sure someone senior sees the ledger.

A protected road runs underneath: structure keeps converting into learning for you, and position into shelter. Mentors appear inside hierarchies, promotions arrive without scandal, and your name gathers weight the slow, durable way. The only hazard is staying past a frame’s worth. Audit the ladder every few years, then climb on.
